# noust_application (Resource)

An application deployed by the server from a git repository. Creating it queues the deployment and waits for the job: the resource exists when the release has passed the health gate, and a deployment that fails is the error you read, with the gate's probes and the journal word for word.

What the API accepts only when the application is made (`source`, `app_type`, `port`, `layout`, `webserver`, `ssl`, `include_www`, `persistent_paths`) replaces the application when it changes; `branch`, `health_check`, the limits, `env_vars` and the team, project and environment are updated in place. A replacement deletes the application and deploys it again, so protect a production application with `deletion_protection` or `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

Needs the permission `apps.manage` (and `apps.operate` for the restart after a change); deleting, and every in-place change, need sudo mode, so the token must be issued with `allow_elevated`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Node.js service deployed from git, behind the health gate, with its limits and variables.
resource "noust_application" "api" {
  domain   = "api.example.com"
  source   = "https://github.com/acme/api.git"
  branch   = "main"
  app_type = "nodejs"

  # The first deployment and every one after it must answer this before a release may serve.
  health_check = {
    path    = "/healthz"
    expect  = "200"
    timeout = 60
  }

  memory_max_mb     = 512
  cpu_quota_percent = 100

  # Only the names listed here are managed: a DATABASE_URL that Noust writes for a linked database stays.
  env_vars = {
    LOG_LEVEL = "info"
    API_KEY   = var.api_key
  }

  # Place it in a team's project and environment.
  team        = "acme"
  project     = "web"
  environment = "production"

  # A production application: Terraform refuses to destroy it until this is false.
  deletion_protection = true
}

variable "api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The application's primary domain, which names it everywhere. Changing it replaces the application.
- `source` (String) The git address to deploy from. Changing it replaces the application.

### Optional

- `app_type` (String) The type of application (`nextjs`, `nodejs`, `python`, `static`...), as `GET /api/apps/types` lists them. Detected from the repository when omitted. Changing it replaces the application.
- `branch` (String) The branch to deploy and to pin: the webhook ignores pushes to any other. It must exist on the remote. Changed in place; removing it from the configuration does not unpin it.
- `cpu_quota_percent` (Number) CPUQuota for the application's unit, in percent of one CPU (200 is two CPUs). `0` removes the limit. Applied in place.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Refuse to destroy the application from Terraform until this is set to `false` and applied. Default `false`.
- `env_vars` (Map of String, Sensitive) Environment variables of the application. Only the names listed here are managed: variables the server sets itself (a linked database's `DATABASE_URL`) or an operator added are left alone. `PORT` and `NODE_ENV` are the unit's and are refused.

The whole map is sensitive. Refreshing compares the values on the server without reading them (a dry run of the merge), so a variable changed by hand shows as a difference.
- `environment` (String) The environment the application belongs to. `production` when omitted. Changing it moves the application.
- `health_check` (Attributes) What the health gate asks of the application before a release may serve. The type's own check when omitted. A static site is checked by its files and refuses one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--health_check))
- `include_www` (Boolean) Also answer on `www.<domain>`, as a redirect to it. `false` when omitted. Only used when the application is made; use `noust_domain` afterwards.
- `layout` (String) `releases` (every deploy is a release behind a health gate, with instant rollback) or `inplace`. The server's `deploy.layout` when omitted. Changing it replaces the application: an in-place application is never converted implicitly.
- `memory_max_mb` (Number) MemoryMax for the application's unit, in MB. `0` removes the limit. Applied in place.
- `persistent_paths` (List of String) Releases layout only: paths, relative to the application, linked into `shared/` and kept across every release (uploads, storage). Only used when the application is made.
- `port` (Number) The port the application listens on. The server picks a free one when omitted. Changing it replaces the application.
- `project` (String) The project the application belongs to. The team's default when omitted. Changing it moves the application.
- `remove_certificate_on_destroy` (Boolean) Also delete the application's certificate when it is destroyed. Default `false`.
- `remove_files_on_destroy` (Boolean) Also delete the application's directory (releases, shared files, uploads) when it is destroyed. Default `false`: the data stays on the server.
- `restart_on_change` (Boolean) Restart the application after a change to `env_vars` or the limits, so the running process picks it up. Default `true`. The restart is not behind the health gate; a deployment is.
- `ssl` (Boolean) Obtain a certificate. `true` when omitted. Only used when the application is made; changing it replaces the application.
- `tasks_max` (Number) TasksMax (processes and threads) for the application's unit, in tasks. `0` removes the limit. Applied in place.
- `team` (String) The team the application belongs to. The one the token works in, its only team or the default when omitted. Changing it moves the application, with its sites, databases and backup schedule.
- `webserver` (String) `nginx` or `apache`. `nginx` when omitted. Only used when the application is made; changing it replaces the application.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The application's domain.
- `unit` (String) The name of the systemd unit that runs the application.

<a id="nestedatt--health_check"></a>
### Nested Schema for `health_check`

Optional:

- `expect` (String) Statuses that mean up, 100 to 599: `200-399`, or `200,204`. Any status below 500 when omitted.
- `interval` (Number) Seconds between two probes, 1 to 60. `2` when omitted.
- `path` (String) Path to probe on `127.0.0.1`, such as `/healthz`. `/` when omitted.
- `retries` (Number) The most probes after the start period, 1 to 100. As many as fit when omitted.
- `start_period` (Number) Seconds during which a failed probe does not count, 0 to 600. `0` when omitted.
- `timeout` (Number) Seconds the gate waits, 5 to 600. `30` when omitted.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# An application already deployed, by its primary domain. Add its configuration, then plan: what the
# server cannot report (the variables' values, ssl, include_www) is adopted from the configuration.
terraform import noust_application.api api.example.com
```
